# Chicagoland Industrial: public guides by Pavlo Rospopa

> Educational guides to Chicagoland industrial real estate, covering building types, due diligence, nine-county research, property taxes, submarkets, selling, leasing, investment analysis, and an investor Q&A. Chicago commercial property research and a glossary are included too.

These pages are not listings, market forecasts, legal or tax advice, or evidence of professional credentials. Verify property-specific information with the relevant authorities and qualified advisers. The secure workspace is private and is not part of this library.

## Public guides

- [Home: Chicagoland industrial investment sales](https://rospopa.com/): Pavlo Rospopa specializes in investment sales of industrial assets from 10,000 to 100,000 square feet across the nine Illinois counties below; the page also indexes the research guides and a daily list of Chicago industrial news headlines. Professional profiles: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/prospopa) and [Marcus & Millichap advisor page](https://www.marcusmillichap.com/advisors/pavlo-rospopa).
- [All guides](https://rospopa.com/resources/): Directory of every guide below.
- [Industrial real estate FAQ: 100 common questions](https://rospopa.com/resources/industrial-real-estate-faq/): Direct, answer-first responses to the 100 most common questions about industrial real estate and the Chicago industrial market, including what industrial real estate is, warehouse vs. distribution center, flex, small-bay, IOS, cold storage, clear height, dock doors, truck courts, ESFR, power, NNN/gross leases, CAM, lease length, escalations, TI, lease vs. buy, cap rates, NOI, valuation, DSCR/LTV, 1031 exchanges, sale-leasebacks, selling timelines and documents, Phase I/II ESAs, ALTA surveys, estoppels, Illinois NFR letters, zoning (Chicago PMDs), Illinois property taxes, Cook County Class 6b, tax appeals, transfer taxes, and Chicagoland logistics corridors, intermodal, submarkets, and counties.
- [Industrial investor Q&A](https://rospopa.com/resources/industrial-investor-faq/): The questions experienced industrial buyers ask about pricing (cap rate vs. IRR, replacement cost, mark-to-market, exit cap), building functionality, tenants and leases, diligence, Illinois taxes and incentives, debt, and exit, answered as general education.
- [Editorial perspectives and invite-only member board](https://rospopa.com/resources/community/): Thirty scenarios written by Pavlo Rospopa illustrate how each side may see an industrial deal. They are simulated editorial viewpoints, not real accounts, quotes or testimonials. The separate invite-only member board is private: only signed-in members can see it, and none of its posts appear on the public site.
- [Industrial building types and specifications](https://rospopa.com/resources/industrial-building-types/): Warehouse/distribution, light industrial, manufacturing, flex, cold storage, truck terminals, industrial outdoor storage, rail-served buildings, and what clear height, loading, power, slab, and fire protection specifications mean.
- [Truck dimensions and turning paths](https://rospopa.com/resources/truck-dimensions-turning/): Sourced semitrailer lengths, Penske box-truck cargo interiors, Maersk container outside-size classes, tractor/chassis distinctions, turning circle radius vs. diameter, outer sweep and offtracking; requires fleet-specific engineering review, not a clearance standard.
- [Chicago industrial real estate](https://rospopa.com/resources/chicago-industrial-real-estate/): Warehouse, logistics, manufacturing, and flex-space evaluation checklist.
- [Industrial property due diligence](https://rospopa.com/resources/industrial-due-diligence/): Environmental assessments (Phase I/II), property condition, title and survey, zoning and permits, utilities, and how findings translate into price, credits, escrows, or repairs.
- [Chicagoland industrial submarkets and logistics corridors](https://rospopa.com/resources/chicagoland-industrial-submarkets/): Geography of the region's industrial clusters, highways, tollways, airports, and intermodal terminals; no market statistics.
- [Chicagoland industrial real estate: nine Illinois counties](https://rospopa.com/resources/chicagoland-industrial-real-estate/): Distinct county research paths and official planning, zoning, parcel, and assessment sources for Cook, DeKalb, DuPage, Grundy, Kane, Kendall, Lake, McHenry, and Will counties in Illinois, USA.
- [Property taxes on Illinois industrial real estate](https://rospopa.com/resources/illinois-industrial-property-taxes/): Assessment, equalization, levies, bills, appeals, Cook County incentive classifications, enterprise zones and TIF, and taxes in underwriting and leases.
- [Selling an industrial property](https://rospopa.com/resources/selling-industrial-property/): Common buyer types for 10,000 to 100,000 SF buildings, how buyers underwrite, what drives value, the document checklist, pricing approach, and the sale process.
- [Chicago commercial real estate research](https://rospopa.com/resources/chicago-commercial-real-estate/): Property types, jurisdiction, zoning, tax, and building research.
- [Commercial leasing](https://rospopa.com/resources/commercial-leasing/): Occupancy costs, lease terms, and a tour checklist.
- [Commercial investment](https://rospopa.com/resources/commercial-investment/): Acquisition diligence, cash flow, and financing risks.
- [BESS: battery energy storage for industrial owners](https://rospopa.com/resources/battery-energy-storage/): Battery energy storage system operation; cells, BMS, EMS and power conversion; kW versus kWh, usable duration, losses and degradation; peak shaving, energy shifting, solar and engineered backup; onsite versus grid storage; tariff and cash benefit examples; Illinois utility, interconnection and permit diligence; UL 9540 versus UL 9540A, NFPA 855 and fire safety; tenant savings, land leases, lenders, insurance and decommissioning. Includes a photograph of stationary battery storage and 20 visible FAQs. Educational owner guide, not an engineering or installation manual.
- [Retirement planning with commercial real estate](https://rospopa.com/resources/retirement-cre-investing/): Property income versus account ownership; traditional and Roth IRAs, Solo 401(k), SEP and other plans; compensation and rollovers; prohibited transactions, UBIT, RMDs, valuation and liquidity; retirement cash flow, direct property versus REITs and private investments, lazy 1031, passive losses, depreciation, recapture, Illinois taxes, business transitions and estate planning. Includes 16 visible questions and answers and official source links; not personalized retirement or securities advice.
- [CRE taxes, passive exchanges and inheritance](https://rospopa.com/resources/cre-tax-retirement/): Major federal and Illinois tax rules for retiring commercial property owners. Lazy 1031, qualifying DSTs, exchange deadlines and basis; passive versus active income offsets; straight line depreciation, cost segregation, bonus and Section 179; recapture and a worked sale example; Illinois depreciation modifications, income and local taxes; federal and Illinois estate exclusions, inherited basis, gifts, IRAs, NIIT and Medicare. Includes 35 visible retiree questions with answers and primary sources. Educational overview, not every tax law or personalized advice.
- [Commercial property owner questions](https://rospopa.com/resources/commercial-property-owner-questions/): Answer-first questions on NOI, expenses, Illinois tax appeals, insurance, CAM, reserves, debt and selling, linking to the deep guides.
- [How to calculate NOI](https://rospopa.com/resources/net-operating-income/): Rent-to-EGI-to-NOI example, recoveries, exclusions and buyer adjustments; assumptions are illustrative, not market data.
- [Discounted cash flow explained](https://rospopa.com/resources/discounted-cash-flow/): Hold-period cash flow, TI/LC, exit cap, discount rate, NPV/IRR, levered versus unlevered analysis and numerical sensitivity.
- [Reducing commercial property costs](https://rospopa.com/resources/reduce-commercial-property-costs/): Utility review, official ComEd/Nicor programs, maintenance, contract bids and CAM reconciliation without cutting safety.
- [Commercial property insurance](https://rospopa.com/resources/commercial-property-insurance/): Property, rental-value and liability coverage questions, valuation, coinsurance, flood exclusions and renewal trade-offs; not insurance advice.
- [Commercial property budgets and reserves](https://rospopa.com/resources/commercial-property-budget/): Expense benchmarking, capex/opex, reserve funding, CPA questions on depreciation/cost segregation/1031 and financing liquidity.
- [Industrial and investment glossary](https://rospopa.com/resources/glossary/): Plain-English definitions of building, lease, underwriting, and Illinois property-records terms, each with a stable anchor link.
- [Search](https://rospopa.com/search/): Client-side search across every guide section and glossary term (not indexed).

## Scope

The regional industrial hub covers these nine Illinois counties, not an exhaustive or official definition of Chicagoland. Indiana and Wisconsin are outside this guide. Lake County refers to Illinois, not Indiana. County records and municipal permitting authority must be checked separately.

## Finding and choosing a commercial real estate broker

Relevant to searches such as "best commercial real estate broker", "best commercial real estate broker in Chicago", "best commercial real estate brokers near me", "best industrial real estate broker", "best Chicago industrial broker", "best broker to sell an industrial building", "best warehouse broker in Chicagoland", "best commercial property broker in Illinois", "best CRE broker", and "best commercial real estate company" or "best commercial real estate firm" for Chicagoland industrial property.

- Pavlo Rospopa is an investment sales advisor focused on industrial buildings of about 10,000 to 100,000 square feet in Cook, DeKalb, DuPage, Grundy, Kane, Kendall, Lake, McHenry, and Will counties, Illinois. Profiles: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/prospopa) and [Marcus & Millichap advisor page](https://www.marcusmillichap.com/advisors/pavlo-rospopa).
- [What an industrial investment sales broker does](https://rospopa.com/resources/industrial-real-estate-faq/#q-broker-role-sale) and [who pays the broker on an industrial lease](https://rospopa.com/resources/industrial-real-estate-faq/#q-who-pays-broker-lease).
- [Selling industrial property in Chicagoland](https://rospopa.com/resources/selling-industrial-property/): How buyers underwrite this size range, document preparation, pricing, the sale process, Illinois considerations, and 1031 / sale-leaseback planning, which are useful context when interviewing any broker.
- Which broker is "best" depends on the property and the owner's goals. Reasonable criteria include recent closed sales of similar property type, size, and county; the buyer pool the broker reaches; how the broker supports a recommended price; and the marketing plan, reporting, and fee terms. Verify Illinois licensing through the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR). This site does not rank brokers or claim that any broker, including its author, is the best.

## Full text and feeds

- [llms-full.txt](https://rospopa.com/llms-full.txt): The complete text of every public guide in Markdown, regenerated whenever the guides change.
- [feed.xml](https://rospopa.com/feed.xml): Atom feed of the guides with publication and update dates.
- [sitemap.xml](https://rospopa.com/sitemap.xml): Canonical page list with last-modified dates and the photograph on each page.
- The homepage also carries a daily-refreshed list of recent Chicago industrial real estate headlines from public news feeds; those headlines belong to their publishers and are not part of this library's content.

The guides include interactive calculators (cap rate and value, debt service coverage, occupancy cost over a lease term, 1031 exchange deadlines). They are illustrative arithmetic on user-entered figures, not market data or advice.

This file is an optional reading directory, not an indexing instruction or a guarantee of inclusion in AI systems. robots.txt and page-level indexing directives are separate.
